cards.title: Discerning the White Thread from the Black Thread at Dawn in Fasting
cards.note: Surah 2:187 permits eating, drinking, and marital relations on fast nights until 'a white thread may be discerned from a black thread at the dawn,' matching the dawn thread test in Mishnah Berakhot 1:2 and Berakhot 9b and fast abstinence in Mishnah Yoma 8:1.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain the white and black threads as a divine metaphor for the streak of daybreak separating from the darkness of night, which some Companions initially took as literal cords until the words 'at the dawn' clarified the rule.
discussion.reply: In Mishnah Berakhot 1:2 (~AD 200) and Talmud Berakhot 9b (~AD 500), the dawn threshold is defined by looking at literal dyed and white wool threads on the ritual fringes (tzitzit) commanded in Numbers 15:38. Because Islamic law lacks the Torah fringe garment that generated the optical wool-thread test, the rabbinic legal rule had to be reinterpreted in Medina as a metaphor for the horizon.

cards.quranEn: It is permitted to you on the night of the fast to have sexual relations with your wives. They are a covering for you, and you are a covering for them. God knows that you have been betraying yourselves (in this regard), and has turned to you (in forgiveness) and pardoned you. So now have relations with them, and seek what God has prescribed for you. And eat and drink, until a white thread may be discerned from a black thread at the dawn. Then keep the fast completely until night, and do not have relations with them while you are devoted to the mosques. Those are the limits (set by) God, so do not go near them. In this way God makes clear His signs to the people, so that they may guard (themselves).
quranHighlights: permitted to you on the night of the fast to have sexual relations with your wives
eat and drink, until a white thread may be discerned from a black thread at the dawn

sources.title: Mishnah Berakhot 1:2
sources.en: From when does one recite Shema in the morning? From when a person can distinguish between sky-blue [tekhelet] and white. Rabbi Eliezer says: From when one can distinguish between sky-blue and leek-green.
highlights: From when a person can distinguish between sky-blue [tekhelet] and white
sources.orig: מֵאֵימָתַי קוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע בְּשַׁחֲרִית. מִשֶּׁיַּכִּיר בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת לְלָבָן. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת לְכַרְתִּי.

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 9b
sources.en: GEMARA: The mishna stated that the time for the recitation of the morning Shema begins when one can distinguish between sky-blue and white. The Gemara asks: To what is between sky-blue and white referring? If you say that it means distinguishing between a pile of white wool and a pile of sky-blue wool, wouldn’t one know the difference at night, as well? Rather, it must be a reference to ritual fringes made with sky-blue strings (see Numbers 15:38) along with white strings, and one must be able to distinguish between the sky-blue strings in the ritual fringes and the white strings in the ritual fringes.
highlights: distinguish between the sky-blue strings in the ritual fringes and the white strings in the ritual fringes
sources.orig: גְּמָ׳ מַאי בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת לְלָבָן? אִילֵּימָא בֵּין גְּבָבָא דְעַמְרָא חִיוָּרָא לִגְבָבָא דְעַמְרָא דִתְכֵלְתָּא — הָא בְּלֵילְיָא נָמֵי מִידָּע יָדְעִי. אֶלָּא, בֵּין תְּכֵלֶת שֶׁבָּהּ לְלָבָן שֶׁבָּהּ.

sources.title: Mishnah Yoma 8:1
sources.en: On Yom Kippur, the day on which there is a mitzva by Torah law to afflict oneself, it is prohibited to engage in eating and in drinking, and in bathing, and in smearing oil on one’s body, and in wearing shoes, and in conjugal relations.

and in conjugal relations

cards.quranAr: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسٞ لَّكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لِبَاسٞ لَّهُنَّۗ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَعَفَا عَنكُمۡۖ فَٱلۡـَٰٔنَ بَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡخَيۡطُ ٱلۡأَبۡيَضُ مِنَ ٱلۡخَيۡطِ ٱلۡأَسۡوَدِ مِنَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّواْ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيۡلِۚ وَلَا تُبَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمۡ عَٰكِفُونَ فِي ٱلۡمَسَٰجِدِۗ تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقۡرَبُوهَاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ

cards.title: Fixed Geographical Direction of Prayer (Qiblah) and Shift from Jerusalem
cards.note: Surah 2:142–145 transitions the community from praying toward Jerusalem to facing the Meccan sanctuary, building on the biblical and rabbinic law of facing Jerusalem in Daniel 6:10, Mishnah Berakhot 4:5, and Talmud Berakhot 30a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators state that praying toward Jerusalem was a temporary divine command in Medina to test who would follow the Prophet, before God restored the primordial Abrahamic sanctuary in Mecca as the permanent direction of prayer.
discussion.reply: Fixing daily prayer toward Jerusalem and its Temple is anchored in 1 Kings 8:44–48, Daniel 6:10, Mishnah Berakhot 4:5 (~AD 200), and Talmud Berakhot 30a (~AD 500). Adopting the Jerusalem prayer orientation upon arriving among Medinan Jewish tribes, and shifting to the Meccan sanctuary roughly sixteen months later after Jewish rejection, tracks the historical realignment of the Medinan polity.

cards.quranEn: [142] The fools among the people will say, ‘What has turned them from the direction (of prayer) which they were (facing) toward?’ Say: ‘The East and the West (belong) to God. He guides whomever He pleases to a straight path.’ [143] In this way We have made you a community (in the) middle, so that you may be witnesses over the people, and that the messenger may be a witness over you. And We established the direction (of prayer) which you were (facing) toward only so that We might know the one who would follow the messenger from the one who would turn back on his heels. Surely it was hard indeed, except for those whom God guided. But God was not one to let your belief go to waste. Surely God is indeed kind (and) compassionate with the people. [144] We do see you turning your face about in the sky, and We shall indeed turn you in a direction which you will be pleased with. Turn your face in the direction of the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces in its direction. Surely those who have been given the Book know indeed that it is the truth from their Lord. God is not oblivious of what they do. [145] Yet even if you bring every sign to those who have been given the Book, they will not follow your direction. You are not a follower of their direction, nor are they followers of each other’s direction. If indeed you follow their (vain) desires, after the knowledge which has come to you, surely then you will indeed be among the evildoers.
quranHighlights: What has turned them from the direction (of prayer) which they were (facing) toward?
Turn your face in the direction of the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces in its direction

sources.en: And when Daniel knew that the decree was ordered, he went into his house; and his windows were opened in his chambers toward Jerusalem, and three times in the day he knelt upon his knees, and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as he used to do before.

sources.title: Mishnah Berakhot 4:5
sources.en: While praying, one must face toward the direction of the Holy Temple. One who was riding on a donkey should dismount and pray calmly. If he is unable to dismount, he should turn his face toward the direction of the Temple. If he is unable to turn his face, it is sufficient that he focus his heart opposite the Holy of Holies.
highlights: While praying, one must face toward the direction of the Holy Temple
he should turn his face toward the direction of the Temple

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 30a
sources.en: One who was standing in prayer in the Diaspora should focus his heart toward Eretz Yisrael, as it is stated: “And they shall pray to You by way of their land which You have given to their fathers” (I Kings 8:48). One who was standing in Eretz Yisrael should focus his heart toward Jerusalem, as it is stated: “And they shall pray to the Lord by way of the city that You have chosen” (I Kings 8:44). One who was standing in Jerusalem should focus his heart toward the Temple, as it is stated: “And they shall pray toward this house” (II Chronicles 6:32). One who was standing in the Temple should focus his heart toward the Holy of Holies, as it is stated: “And they shall pray toward this place” (I Kings 8:35).

cards.quranAr: ۞سَيَقُولُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَا وَلَّىٰهُمۡ عَن قِبۡلَتِهِمُ ٱلَّتِي كَانُواْ عَلَيۡهَاۚ قُل لِّلَّهِ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقُ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبُۚ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٖ ﴿142﴾ وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةٗ وَسَطٗا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدٗاۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿143﴾ قَدۡ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجۡهِكَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبۡلَةٗ تَرۡضَىٰهَاۚ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُونَ ﴿144﴾ وَلَئِنۡ أَتَيۡتَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِكُلِّ ءَايَةٖ مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبۡلَتَكَۚ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِتَابِعٖ قِبۡلَتَهُمۡۚ وَمَا بَعۡضُهُم بِتَابِعٖ قِبۡلَةَ بَعۡضٖۚ وَلَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتَ أَهۡوَآءَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِنَّكَ إِذٗا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ ﴿145﴾

cards.title: Polygamy Cap of Four Wives ('Two, or Three, or Four') and Talmud Yevamot 44a
cards.note: Surah 4:3 caps a man's concurrent wives at four ('two, or three, or four'), matching the rabbinic legal limit in Talmud Bavli Yevamot 44a restricting marriage to a maximum of four wives so each receives her conjugal right.

discussion.view: Muslim jurists explain that pre-Islamic Arabs married without numerical limit, and that Surah 4:3 revealed a divine ceiling of four wives conditioned on equitable treatment and financial maintenance.
discussion.reply: The Hebrew Bible sets no four-wife limit for ordinary Israelites. The exact ceiling of four concurrent wives originates as post-biblical rabbinic halakhah in Talmud Bavli Yevamot 44a (~AD 500), where the sages derive the number four from the husband's weekly conjugal obligation so that each wife receives her marital right at least once a month.

cards.quranEn: If you fear that you will not act fairly toward the orphan girls, marry what seems good to you of the women: two, or three, or four. But if you fear that you will not be fair, (marry only) one, or what your right (hands) own. That (will make it) more likely that you will not be biased.
quranHighlights: marry what seems good to you of the women: two, or three, or four
if you fear that you will not be fair, (marry only) one

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Yevamot
sources.ref: Yevamot 44a (Rabbinic Cap of Up to Four Wives)
sources.en: The Gemara explains: The mishna teaches us good advice; in a case of up to four women, yes, if he can provide for them then it is acceptable to marry all of them. But if there are any more than that, no, he should not, in order that he will be able to meet the conjugal rights of each woman at least once in each month. A Torah scholar is expected to provide conjugal relations once a week. If he marries no more than four women, then that will ensure that each of his wives will receive their conjugal rights at least once a month.
highlights: in a case of up to four women, yes, if he can provide for them then it is acceptable to marry all of them
If he marries no more than four women, then that will ensure that each of his wives will receive their conjugal rights

cards.title: Three Talmudic Prayer Rules: Intoxication, Seminal Washing, and Soil Wiping
cards.note: Surah 4:43 combines three ritual rules for prayer in one verse—not praying while drunk, bathing after seminal impurity, and wiping with clean soil when lacking water after relieving oneself—matching Eruvin 64a, Berakhot 22a, and Berakhot 15a.

discussion.view: Islamic jurisprudence views these three rulings as direct divine legislation revealed in Medina to regulate ritual purity (taharah) and sober mindfulness before standing in prayer, with dry earth wiping (tayammum) granted as a prophetic dispensation.
discussion.reply: While Leviticus 15:16 requires bathing after seminal emission, the specific dispensation to wipe the hands with earth, a pebble, or wood chips when water is unavailable after relieving oneself before prayer is a post-biblical rabbinic ordinance recorded in Talmud Berakhot 15a (~AD 500), alongside the seminal water-shortage rule in Berakhot 22a and the intoxication prayer ban in Eruvin 64a.

cards.quranEn: You who believe! Do not go near the prayer when you are drunk, until you know what you are saying, or (when you are) defiled, unless (you are) travelers (on the) way, until you wash yourselves. If you are sick or on a journey, or if one of you has come from the toilet, or if you have touched women, and you do not find any water, take clean soil and wipe your faces and your hands. Surely God is pardoning, forgiving.
quranHighlights: Do not go near the prayer when you are drunk
or (when you are) defiled, unless (you are) travelers (on the) way, until you wash yourselves
you do not find any water, take clean soil and wipe your faces and your hands

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Eruvin
sources.en: Rabba bar Rav Huna said: One who has drunk wine must not pray, but if he nonetheless prayed, his prayer is a prayer, i.e., he has fulfilled his obligation. On the other hand, one who is intoxicated with wine must not pray, and if he prayed, his prayer is an abomination.
highlights: one who is intoxicated with wine must not pray, and if he prayed, his prayer is an abomination
sources.orig: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: שָׁתוּי אַל יִתְפַּלֵּל, וְאִם הִתְפַּלֵּל — תְּפִלָּתוֹ תְּפִלָּה. שִׁיכּוֹר אַל יִתְפַּלֵּל, וְאִם הִתְפַּלֵּל — תְּפִלָּתוֹ תּוֹעֵבָה.

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Berakhot
sources.ref: Berakhot 22a (Seminal Impurity and Lacking Water for Immersion)
sources.en: When Rav Dimi came from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia, he said: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehuda Gelostera said: The halakha that one who experienced a seminal emission can be purified by pouring nine kav was only taught for a sick person who experienced the emission involuntarily. However, a sick person who experienced a normal seminal emission in the course of marital relations, is required to immerse himself in forty se’a.

seminal emission in the course of marital relations, is required to immerse himself

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Berakhot
sources.ref: Berakhot 15a (Wiping Hands with Earth When Lacking Water)
sources.en: Ravina said to Rava: My Master, look at this Torah scholar [tzurva merabbanan] who came from Eretz Yisrael and said something astonishing: One who has no water with which to wash his hands, it is sufficient that he wipes his hands with earth, a rock, or a sliver of wood. Rava replied to Ravina: He spoke well, as, is it written: I will wash with water? In purity, is written referring to anything that cleans, as Rav Ḥisda would curse one who went out of his way to seek water at the time of prayer.
highlights: One who has no water with which to wash his hands, it is sufficient that he wipes his hands with earth

cards.title: Three-Period Post-Divorce Waiting Term ('Iddah) to Ascertain Pregnancy
cards.note: Surah 2:228 requires divorced women to wait three periods before remarrying so as not to conceal what is in their wombs, matching the three-month waiting period and paternity rationale in Mishnah Yevamot 4:10.

discussion.view: Muslim jurists view the three-cycle waiting period ('iddah) as a revealed legal measure ensuring paternity certainty and giving estranged spouses a structured window for reconciliation.
discussion.reply: The Mosaic Torah contains no three-month post-divorce waiting rule. The mandatory three-month waiting period before a divorced or widowed woman may remarry—along with its explicit rationale of ascertaining pregnancy and paternity—was codified centuries earlier in Mishnah Yevamot 4:10 (~AD 200) and Talmud Bavli Yevamot 42b (~AD 500).

cards.quranEn: (Let) the divorced women wait by themselves for three periods. It is not permitted to them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, if they believe in God and the Last Day. Their husbands have a better right to take them back in that (period), if they wish to set (things) right. Women rightfully have the same privilege (as is exercised) over them, but men have a rank above them. God is mighty, wise.
quranHighlights: (Let) the divorced women wait by themselves for three periods
It is not permitted to them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

sources.title: Mishnah Yevamot 4:10
sources.en: A yevama may neither perform ḥalitza nor enter into levirate marriage until she has waited three months from the time of her husband’s death. And similarly, all other women may not be betrothed and may not marry until they have waited three months since their previous marriage ended. This waiting period is necessary so that, should a woman give birth shortly after remarrying, it will be obvious who the father of the child is. This applies both to virgins and non-virgins, both to divorcées and widows, and both to women who were married to their previous husbands and women who were only betrothed. All of these women must wait three months before remarrying even though for some of them the reason for doing so does not apply.
highlights: may not marry until they have waited three months since their previous marriage ended
should a woman give birth shortly after remarrying, it will be obvious who the father of the child is
both to divorcées and widows

cards.title: Fourfold Dietary Prohibition and the Life-Saving Necessity Exemption
cards.note: Surah 2:173 forbids carrion, blood, swine flesh, and idol-dedicated meat while exempting those forced by life-saving necessity, combining Acts 15:28–29, Leviticus 11:7–8, and Talmud Yoma 82a (pikuach nefesh).

discussion.view: Islamic theology regards the prohibition of carrion, blood, pork, and idol-consecrated meat—paired with mercy for one forced by starvation—as the original prophetic dietary law perfected in the Quran.
discussion.reply: Whereas the Mosaic Torah lists dozens of forbidden land, sea, and winged creatures in Leviticus 11, the compact fourfold list of idol-sacrificed meat, blood, carrion/strangled animals, and pork reproduces the Apostolic Decree of Acts 15:28–29 as observed by Late Antique Eastern Christians, combined with the rabbinic life-saving necessity exemption (pikuach nefesh) codified in Talmud Yoma 82a.

cards.quranEn: He has only forbidden to you: the dead (animal), and the blood, and swine’s flesh, and what has been dedicated to (a god) other than God. But whoever is forced (by necessity), not desiring or (deliberately) transgressing – no sin (rests) on him. Surely God is forgiving, compassionate.

cards.title: The Fixed Two-Full-Year (Twenty-Four-Month) Breastfeeding Term
cards.note: Surah 2:233 stipulates that mothers shall nurse their children for two full years (24 months) while fathers provide maintenance or hire a wet nurse, matching the exact 24-month nursing term in Talmud Ketubot 60a and 59b.

discussion.view: Islamic family law treats the two-year nursing term and the father's duty to compensate a divorced mother or wet nurse as divine legislation revealed to protect infant welfare and maternal rights.
discussion.reply: Neither the Hebrew Bible nor the New Testament legislates a fixed two-year nursing period. Talmud Bavli Ketubot 60a (~AD 500) establishes the exact twenty-four-month statutory nursing term, and Ketubot 59b pairs it with the legal rule requiring a divorced father to pay a wet-nurse wage if the infant recognizes its mother.

cards.quranEn: Mothers shall nurse their children for two full years, for those who wish to complete the nursing (period). (It is an obligation) on the father for him (to supply) their provision and their clothing rightfully. No one is to be burdened beyond their capacity. A mother is not to suffer on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child. The (father’s) heir has a similar (obligation) to that. If the two of them wish, by mutual consent and consultation, to wean (the child earlier), (there is) no blame on (either of) them. And if you wish to seek nursing for your children, (there is) no blame on you, provided you pay what you have rightfully promised. Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that God sees what you do.

(It is an obligation) on the father for him (to supply) their provision and their clothing rightfully
if you wish to seek nursing for your children, (there is) no blame on you, provided you pay what you have rightfully promised

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud, Ketubot 60a
sources.en: The Sages taught in a baraita: A child may continue to nurse until the age of twenty-four months, and from this point forward, if he continues to nurse, he is like one who nurses from a non-kosher animal, as a woman’s milk is forbidden to anyone other than a small child; this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. Rabbi Yehoshua says: A child may continue to nurse even for four or five years, and this is permitted. However, if he ceased, i.e., was weaned, after twenty-four months and then resumed nursing, he is like one who nurses from a non-kosher animal.
highlights: A child may continue to nurse until the age of twenty-four months

cards.title: Friday Congregational Prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) and Leaving Market Trade
cards.note: Surah 62:9–11 commands believers to leave trade when called to prayer on Friday (Yawm al-Jumu'ah), paralleling the Friday-eve horn blasts in Talmud Bavli Shabbat 35b sounded to halt work in the city and instruct shopkeepers to close their stores.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators state that God chose Friday for the weekly congregational assembly and prohibited commercial transactions during the midday call and prayer, distinguishing Islam from the full-day Jewish Sabbath rest.
discussion.reply: In pre-Islamic Medina, Friday was known in Jewish Aramaic as Arubat Shabbat (the eve of Sabbath), when market preparation concluded before sunset. Talmud Bavli Shabbat 35b (~AD 500) mandates sounding signals on Friday afternoon specifically to halt city work and close shops, providing the exact weekly Friday market-cessation framework adapted in Surah 62:9–11.

cards.quranEn: [9] You who believe! When the call to prayer is made on the day of assembly, hurry to the remembrance of God, and leave business aside. That is better for you, if (only) you knew. [10] Then, when the prayer is finished, disperse on the earth and seek some favor from God, and remember God often, so that you may prosper. [11] But when they see (the chance of) some (business) transaction or diversion, they rush off to it, and leave you standing. Say: ‘What is with God is better than any diversion or transaction. God is the best of providers.’

The first blast is in order to stop the people from work in the fields. The second blast is to stop those who are working in the city, and to inform the proprietors to close the stores.

cards.title: Fixed Daily Prayers from the Declining of the Sun to Nightfall and Night Vigil
cards.note: Surah 17:78–79 prescribes ritual prayer from the declining of the sun until nightfall, the dawn recitation, and keeping a night vigil (tahajjud), matching the daily prayer windows in Mishnah Berakhot 4:1 and David's midnight psalm vigil in Talmud Berakhot 3b.

discussion.view: Islamic scholarship reads Surah 17:78–79 as encompassing the five daily prayers ordained during the Prophet's night journey alongside the voluntary night vigil (tahajjud) practiced by the righteous.
discussion.reply: Fixed daily prayer windows governed by solar transitions—morning, afternoon decline until nightfall, and night—were codified in Mishnah Berakhot 4:1 (~AD 200), while rising during a portion of the night for supererogatory psalm recitation and praise parallels David's midnight vigil in Talmud Bavli Berakhot 3b (~AD 500) and Late Antique monastic night watches.

cards.quranEn: [78] Observe the prayer at the setting of the sun until the darkness of the night, and (deliver) a recitation at the dawn – surely a recitation at the dawn is witnessed. [79] And a part of the night – keep watch in it as a gift for you. It may be that your Lord will raise you up to a praised position.
quranHighlights: Observe the prayer at the setting of the sun until the darkness of the night, and (deliver) a recitation at the dawn
And a part of the night – keep watch in it

sources.title: Mishnah Berakhot.4.1
sources.en: According to the Rabbis, the morning prayer may be recited until noon. Rabbi Yehuda says: It may be recited only until four hours after sunrise. According to the Rabbis, the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening. Rabbi Yehuda says: It may be recited only until the midpoint of the afternoon [pelag haminḥa], i.e., the midpoint of the period that begins with the sacrifice of the daily afternoon offering and ends at nightfall, which is the end of the afternoon. The evening prayer may be recited throughout the night and is not fixed to a specific hour.
highlights: the morning prayer may be recited until noon
the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening
The evening prayer may be recited throughout the night

cards.title: Ritual Ablution (Wudu'): Washing Face, Forearms, Head, and Feet Before Prayer
cards.note: Surah 5:6 codifies the four-part pre-prayer ablution (washing face and forearms to elbows, wiping head and feet to ankles) and dry soil wiping (tayammum), paralleling Exodus 30:19–21 and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 15a.

discussion.view: Sunni and Shi'i jurists treat Surah 5:6 as the comprehensive Medinan charter for minor ritual ablution (wudu'), major ritual bathing (ghusl), and dry earth purification (tayammum) prior to canonical prayer.
discussion.reply: Washing the hands and feet with water before approaching sacred service is commanded in Exodus 30:19–21, and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 15a (~AD 500) extends this priestly washing to every layperson after relieving oneself before reciting the Shema and Amidah—adding the exact rabbinic rule that one lacking water wipes the hands with earth or a pebble.

cards.quranEn: You who believe! When you stand up for the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles. If you are defiled, purify yourselves. If you are sick or on a journey, or if one of you has come from the toilet, or if you have touched women, and you do not find any water, take clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it. God does not wish to place any difficulty on you, but He wishes to purify you and to complete His blessing on you, so that you may be thankful.

if one of you has come from the toilet, or if you have touched women, and you do not find any water, take clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Berakhot
sources.ref: Berakhot 15a (Washing Hands Before Prayer or Wiping with Earth)
sources.en: Anyone who relieves himself, washes his hands, dons phylacteries, recites Shema, and prays, the verse ascribes credit to him as if he built an altar and offered a sacrifice upon it, as it is written: “I will wash in purity my hands, and I will encircle the altar of the Lord” (Psalms 26:6). Rava said to him: Do you not maintain, Master, that one who does so, it is as if he immersed his entire body, as it is written: “I will wash in purity,” and it is not written: “I will wash my hands”? Ravina said to Rava: My Master, look at this Torah scholar [tzurva merabbanan] who came from Eretz Yisrael and said something astonishing: One who has no water with which to wash his hands, it is sufficient that he wipes his hands with earth, a rock, or a sliver of wood.

cards.title: Three-Month Divorce Waiting Period ('Iddah) for Postmenopausal and Minor Wives
cards.note: Surah 65:1–4 prescribes a three-month waiting period ('iddah) for women past menstruation and wives who have not menstruated, and delivery for pregnant women, paralleling Mishnah Yevamot 4:10 and Talmud Yevamot 42b.

discussion.view: Classical commentators explain that Surah 65:4 was revealed when Medinan believers asked about the waiting period of older women, young brides who had not menstruated, and pregnant wives whose terms were not specified in Surah 2:228.
discussion.reply: Talmud Bavli Yevamot 42b (~AD 500), commenting on Mishnah Yevamot 4:10, records Rabbi Meir's ruling that the three-month post-divorce waiting period applies equally to an elderly postmenopausal woman (zekenah) and a prepubescent minor bride (ketannah). Surah 65:4 codifies Rabbi Meir's exact two non-menstruating categories under the same three-month rule.

cards.quranEn: [1] Prophet! When you divorce women, divorce them when they have reached (the end of) their waiting period. Count the waiting period, and guard (yourselves) against God your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor let them leave, unless they commit clear immorality. Those are the limits (set by) God. Whoever transgresses the limits (set by) God has done himself evil. You do not know, perhaps after that God may bring about a new situation. [2] When they reach their term, either retain them rightfully, or part from them rightfully. Call in two of your just men as witnesses, and conduct the witnessing (as if) before God. That is what anyone who believes in God and the Last Day is admonished. Whoever guards (himself) against God – He will make a way out for him, [3] and will provide for him from where he was not expecting. Whoever puts his trust in God – He will be enough for him. Surely God attains his purpose. God has appointed a measure for everything. [4] (As for) those of your women who have no hope of (further) menstruation: if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and (also for) those who have not (yet) menstruated. (As for) those who are pregnant, their term (is) when they deliver what they bear. Whoever guards (himself) against God – He will bring about some relief for him from His command.
quranHighlights: those of your women who have no hope of (further) menstruation: if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and (also for) those who have not (yet) menstruated

sources.title: Mishnah Yevamot
sources.en: A yevama may neither perform ḥalitza nor enter into levirate marriage until she has waited three months from the time of her husband’s death. And similarly, all other women may not be betrothed and may not marry until they have waited three months since their previous marriage ended. This waiting period is necessary so that, should a woman give birth shortly after remarrying, it will be obvious who the father of the child is. This applies both to virgins and non-virgins, both to divorcées and widows, and both to women who were married to their previous husbands and women who were only betrothed. All of these women must wait three months before remarrying even though for some of them the reason for doing so does not apply.
highlights: all other women may not be betrothed and may not marry until they have waited three months since their previous marriage ended

cards.title: Guarding the Middle Prayer (Salat al-Wusta) and Praying Riding in Fear
cards.note: Surah 2:238–239 commands guarding the daily prayers, especially 'the middle prayer,' and praying on foot or riding when in fear, matching the afternoon prayer vigilance in Talmud Berakhot 6b and the danger and riding prayer rules in Mishnah Berakhot 4:4–5.

discussion.view: Hadith collections and commentators identify 'the middle prayer' primarily with the afternoon prayer ('Asr) and cite Surah 2:239 as the scriptural basis for the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf) on foot or horseback.
discussion.reply: Talmud Bavli Berakhot 6b (~AD 500) singles out the afternoon prayer (Minhah) for special vigilance because of midday commercial distractions, while Mishnah Berakhot 4:4–5 (~AD 200) explicitly legislates how a traveler walking in a place of danger or riding an animal performs a shortened prayer without dismounting.

cards.quranEn: [238] Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer. And stand before God obedient. [239] If you fear (danger), (pray) on foot or (while) riding. But when you are secure, remember God, since He has taught you what you did not know.
quranHighlights: Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer
If you fear (danger), (pray) on foot or (while) riding

May their needs be before You. Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.
highlights: One who cannot recite a complete prayer because he is walking in a place of danger, recites a brief prayer

sources.title: Mishnah Berakhot
sources.en: While praying, one must face toward the direction of the Holy Temple. One who was riding on a donkey should dismount and pray calmly. If he is unable to dismount, he should turn his face toward the direction of the Temple. If he is unable to turn his face, it is sufficient that he focus his heart opposite the Holy of Holies.
highlights: One who was riding on a donkey should dismount and pray calmly. If he is unable to dismount, he should turn his face

cards.title: Prescribed Fasting with Make-Up Days for Sickness or Travel
cards.note: Surah 2:183–185 prescribes fasting 'as it was prescribed for those before you' and allows the sick or travelers to make up missed days later, combining Numbers 9:10–11, Mishnah Yoma 8:5, and pre-Islamic 'Ashura fasting in Bukhari 4504.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes state that God prescribed fasting for earlier prophetic communities and transitioned the Muslim community from the earlier fast of 'Ashura to the month of Ramadan with merciful exemptions for illness and travel.
discussion.reply: Surah 2:183 explicitly appeals to the precedent of earlier communities ('as it was prescribed for those who were before you'). Its rule allowing a traveler to postpone the fast to an equal count of later days mirrors the Second Passover travel-postponement law of Numbers 9:10–11, combined with the illness exemption of Mishnah Yoma 8:5 and the pre-Islamic/Jewish 'Ashura fast in Sahih al-Bukhari 4504.

cards.quranEn: [183] You who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those who were before you, so that you may guard (yourselves). [184] (Fast for) a number of days. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. And for those who can afford it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person. Whoever does good voluntarily – it is better for him. But to fast is better for you, if (only) you knew. [185] The month of Ramaḍān, in which the Qur’ān was sent down as a guidance for the people, and as clear signs of the guidance and the Deliverance: so whoever of you is present during the month, let him fast in it, but whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. God wishes to make it easy for you, and does not wish any hardship for you. And (He wishes) that you should fulfill the number (of days), and that you should magnify God for having guided you, and that you should be thankful.
quranHighlights: Fasting is prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those who were before you
Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days

sources.title: Mishnah Yoma 8:5
sources.en: If a person is ill and requires food due to potential danger, one feeds him according to the advice of medical experts who determine that he indeed requires food. highlights: If a person is ill and requires food due to potential danger, one feeds him

cards.title: Establishing Prayer at the Two Ends of the Day and Approaches of Night
cards.note: Surah 11:114 enjoins performing ritual prayer (al-salat) 'at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,' mirroring the three daily prayer times in Talmud Bavli Berakhot 26b and Psalm 55:17 (LXX 54:17).

discussion.view: Commentators interpret 'the two ends of the day' as the dawn and afternoon prayers and 'the approaches of the night' as the evening and night prayers, seeing the Meccan verse as an early stage of the five daily prayers.
discussion.reply: Before the five-prayer schedule was formalized in later tradition, Surah 11:114 describes a three-part daily liturgical cycle—morning, late afternoon, and early night—that corresponds directly to the three daily prayers (evening, morning, and afternoon) of Psalm 55:17 (LXX 54:17) and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 26b.

cards.quranEn: And observe the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Surely good (deeds) take away evil (ones). That is a reminder to the mindful.
quranHighlights: observe the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Berakhot 26b (Three Daily Prayers Instituted by the Patriarchs)
sources.workSub: Three Daily Prayers Instituted by the Patriarchs
sources.en: Why did the Rabbis say that the morning prayer may be recited until noon? Because, although the daily morning offering is typically brought early in the morning, it may be sacrificed until noon. And Rabbi Yehuda says: My opinion, that the morning prayer may be recited until four hours into the day, is because the daily morning offering is sacrificed until four hours. And why did the Rabbis say that the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening? Because the daily afternoon offering is sacrificed until the evening. Rabbi Yehuda says that the afternoon prayer may be recited only until the midpoint of the afternoon because, according to his opinion, the daily afternoon offering is sacrificed until the midpoint of the afternoon. And why did they say that the evening prayer is not fixed? Because the burning of the limbs and fats of the offerings that were not consumed by the fire on the altar until the evening.
highlights: the morning prayer may be recited until noon
the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening
the evening prayer is not fixed
